slo_title: Apply branching and decision-making constructs to control program flow based on conditions.

Which keyword is used to skip the current iteration of a loop and proceed to the next one?
Which of the following is a branching statement in Java?
Which construct is best suited when a condition needs to be checked before executing the loop body?
Which decision-making structure is most appropriate for choosing one out of many fixed options?

sq.q: Differentiate between the while and do-while loops in Java.
answer: In a while loop, the condition is checked before executing the loop body. If the condition is false at the start, the body may not execute at all. In a do-while loop, the loop body is executed at least once before checking the condition.

sq.q: Write a Java code snippet using a for loop to print the even numbers from 1 to 10.
answer: for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i++) { if (i % 2 == 0) { System.out.print(i + " "); } } This loop checks if the number is divisible by 2 and prints only the even numbers.

lq.q: A ticketing system gives discounts based on the customer's age and trip type. The rules are: If the age is below 12, they get a 50% discount. If the age is 60 or above, they get a 30% discount. If the trip is a "round-trip", an additional 10% discount is applied to all categories. Write a Java program to calculate and display the final discount percentage based on these rules. Also explain the logic used for branching and decision making.
answer: Program: import java.util.Scanner; public class TicketDiscount { public static void main(String[] args) { Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in); System.out.print("Enter age: "); int age = sc.nextInt(); System.out.print("Is it a round-trip? (yes/no): "); String tripType = sc.next(); double discount = 0; if (age < 12) { discount = 50; } else if (age >= 60) { discount = 30; } if (tripType.equalsIgnoreCase("yes")) { discount += 10; } System.out.println("Final Discount: " + discount + "%"); } } Explanation of Logic: Branching (if-else) is used to determine the age-based discount. A second independent if adds a 10% discount for round-trips. This demonstrates clear separation of conditions and compound logic using decision-making constructs. It also reflects real-world rule-based programming, where multiple conditions can independently affect an outcome.
